Wow, wow, wow Fudge is by far the best AI builder I have tried—and I have tested many well-known and lesser-known page builders. Don’t let the number of reviews fool you. Many other apps ask for a review only a few hours after installation. Fudge never asked me for anything; I genuinely felt that I had to write this review myself. That says a lot about their professionalism. As the name suggests, Fudge Agent works almost like having your own web design and SEO agency. You simply explain what you want in a sentence, and the agent handles the task. For larger or more complicated jobs, you do not have to sit and wait in front of the screen. You receive an email when the work is completed. Another major advantage is that Fudge does not leave unnecessary code and clutter in your theme if you decide to remove the app. You can also make manual adjustments yourself whenever needed. In summary, Fudge allows you to manage design, navigation, SEO and many other improvements almost entirely on your own with one app. I definitely recommend giving it some time—you will quickly understand what makes it different from the others.

The design process with Fudge worked well overall, and I am happy with the final result. Unfortunately, I believe the pricing model is completely unreasonable for smaller Shopify stores. I spent a considerable amount of time designing my store step by step and making numerous adjustments. Only when everything was finished and I wanted to publish the result did it become clear that a paid subscription costing $79 per month was required. For a single publication or occasional changes, this price is far too high. What I find particularly disappointing is that there is no affordable option to publish a completed design just once. Many users do not need an ongoing AI service or 100,000 credits every month. They simply want to transfer their finished design to Shopify. Requiring them to pay $79 every month is not customer-friendly. A fairer pricing model could include: • A one-time publishing fee • An affordable plan for small stores • A pay-per-publish option • A $10–$20 monthly plan with fewer credits It should also be made clear before users begin designing that publishing requires a paid subscription. If this only becomes apparent at the end, users may understandably feel pressured to pay because they have already invested considerable time and effort into their design. The product itself has potential and can produce good results. However, due to the expensive publishing paywall and the lack of an affordable option for occasional users, I can currently only recommend it with significant reservations to small or new Shopify businesses. I genuinely hope Fudge reconsiders its pricing model and introduces a fairer option for users who only need to make and publish occasional changes.
